Set up the Julia backend

Source: R/ctJuliaInstall.R
ctJuliaInstall.Rd

Installs everything ctFit(backend='julia') needs, in one call and without restarting R: the JuliaConnectoR package, Julia, and the Julia packages that the engine shipped with ctsem depends on. Steps that are already done are skipped, so on a machine that already has Julia this only prepares the engine.

Usage

ctJuliaInstall(
  threads = NULL,
  version = NULL,
  agree = NULL,
  force = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

threads

Number of Julia threads. Julia fixes this when it starts, so it applies to the session this call starts (see ctJuliaSetup).

version

Julia version to install. Defaults to the version the engine shipped with ctsem was tested with. The download is checksum-verified only for that default.

agree

TRUE to consent to the installs without being asked, FALSE to refuse them. NULL, the default, asks in an interactive session and refuses otherwise.

force

Reinstall Julia even if one is already available, and restart any running Julia session.

quiet

Suppress download and installation progress output.

Value

A Julia-engine status list, invisibly; see ctJuliaStatus.

Details

Each step that installs something asks first, naming the download and where it goes. In a non-interactive session nothing is installed unless agree = TRUE or the environment variable CTSEM_JULIA_AGREE=yes is set.

Julia is downloaded only if none can be found. ctsem looks in JULIA_BINDIR, then at a Julia it installed itself, then on the PATH, then among juliaup's installations. A Julia that ctsem installs goes under tools::R_user_dir("ctsem", "data"), and later sessions find it without any environment variable. The PATH and shell profile are left unchanged. To use a different Julia afterwards, set JULIA_BINDIR.

See also

ctJuliaSetup, ctJuliaStatus

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ctJuliaInstall()            # ask, then install whatever is missing
ctJuliaInstall(threads = 4) # and start the Julia session with four threads
} # }
